'''Homi Nusserwanji Sethna''' (24 August 1923&nbsp;– 5 September 2010) was an Indian [[Nuclear physics|nuclear scientist]] and a [[chemical engineer]], gaining international fame as the Chairman of the [[Atomic Energy Commission of India|Atomic Energy Commission]] (India) during the time when the first nuclear test, codename ''[[Smiling Buddha]]'' in [[Pokhran|Pokhran Test Range]] in 1974 was conducted.<ref name="tt">{{cite news|url=http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2010-09-07/india/28228588_1_homi-nusserwanji-sethna-nuclear-test-pokhran|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103090031/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2010-09-07/india/28228588_1_homi-nusserwanji-sethna-nuclear-test-pokhran|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 November 2012|title=Homi Sethna, nuclear legend, passes away|date=7 Sep 2010|first1=Srinivas|work=[[The Times of India]]|last1=Laxman}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://hindu.com/2010/09/07/stories/2010090755671300.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100910013653/http://hindu.com/2010/09/07/stories/2010090755671300.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=10 September 2010|title=Homi Sethna passes away|date=7 Sep 2010|work=[[The Hindu]]|location=Chennai, India}}</ref> He was the primary and central figure in India's civilian nuclear program as well as the construction of nuclear power plants. In 1991, he was appointed as [[Sheriff of Mumbai]].

He was awarded the second highest civilian award the [[Padma Vibhushan]] in 1975, by [[Government of India]].

Earlier in his career, he had full technical responsibility for setting up of the [[Thorium]] extraction plant at [[Aluva|Alwaye]], [[Kerala]] India, for separation of rare earth from [[monazite]] sands.

==Early life and education==
Homi Sethna was born to a [[Parsis|Parsi]] family on 24 August 1923 in [[Mumbai|Bombay]] (now Mumbai).<ref>{{cite news|title=Dr Homi Sethna: The man who powered India's nuclear dream|url=https://www.rediff.com/news/report/homi-sethna-he-powered-indias-nuke-dream/20100906.htm|access-date=10 February 2018|work=Rediff.com|date=6 September 2010}}</ref> He did his schooling from [[St. Xavier's High School, Fort]], [[Mumbai|Bombay]].<ref>[http://www.xaviersfort.org/history/headlines.asp Notable alumni] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081203144253/http://www.xaviersfort.org/history/headlines.asp |date=3 December 2008 }} ''[[St. Xavier's High School, Fort]]''  - Official website.</ref> He studied [[chemical engineering]] at [[Institute of Chemical Technology|University Department of Chemical Technology]] and the [[University of Michigan]] [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]].

Homi Sethna's younger brother was the noted lawyer Rusi Sethna. Incidentally, Rusi Sethna's daughter, Behrouz Mistry, is the wife of Shapoorji Mistry, elder son of [[Pallonji Mistry]] and elder brother of [[Cyrus Mistry]].

==Career==
He was formerly Chairman of [[Atomic Energy Commission of India|Atomic Energy Commission]], in 1976 he became the first chairman of [[Maharashtra Academy of Sciences]], located in [[Pune]], Maharashtra.

===Head of Trombay Nuclear Facility===
He completed the construction of the [[Thorium]] plant and the plant for the production of nuclear grade [[uranium]] metal at [[Trombay]], India. His first major challenging assignment was the setting up of the [[Plutonium]] Plant at Trombay in 1959. This was designed and constructed entirely by Indian scientists and engineers under H. N. Sethna as the Project Engineer. The [[Jaduguda uranium mine|Uranium Mill]] at [[Jadugora|Jaduguda]], Jharkhand was also constructed under his guidance in 1967. He was also the Project Manager of a 40 MW reactor called Canada-India Reactor in 1956–58.

===Indian atomic test of 1974===
He was the guiding force behind the first peaceful nuclear explosion, [[Smiling Buddha|Project Smiling Buddha]] in India on 18 May 1974,<ref>[https://us.rediff.com/news/2006/jan/27inter1.htm 'He visualised a lively picture of a powerful India' -  Interview/Dr Homi Sethna] ''[[Rediff.com]]'', 27 January 2006.</ref> and in 1975, Homi Sethna, then chairman of the [[Atomic Energy Commission of India|Atomic Energy Commission]], [[Raja Ramanna]] and [[Basanti Dulal Nagchaudhuri]] (head of the [[Defence Research and Development Organisation|DRDO]]) received the [[Padma Vibhushan]].
